steps: Set the Juno-106 to the same MIDI channel as your bandmate's (see the MIDI channel section of the owner's manual).
On the back panel, set the MIDI function switch to position III, so it sends and receives sysex as well as notes and controllers.
Leave the switch at III: every slider and switch move then goes out and comes in as a sysex message on its own.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (the Juno-106 has no USB).
To share a stored patch, select it and the Juno-106 sends it. To share the sound the sliders are set to right now, press MANUAL.
If a slider sends values on its own, clean or replace it before you jam, or it will keep changing your bandmate's sound.
In the MIDI functions, set the Alpha Juno's MIDI channel to the one your app uses.
In the MIDI functions, turn on system exclusive (sysex), so it sends and receives tone data.
With sysex on, edits you make with the alpha dial go out as sysex messages.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (no USB).
There's no 'send' button: write your edited tone to a memory, then select that tone. Selecting it sends the whole tone to your bandmate.
Set the JX-8P's MIDI channel to the one your app uses (see the MIDI section of the owner's manual).
Turn on its MIDI exclusive (sysex) setting, so tone data is sent and received.
With sysex on, PG-800 programmer and panel edits go out as sysex messages.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (no USB).
To send your sound, write your edits to a tone memory, then select that tone. The JX-8P sends the whole tone when it's selected.
Set the MIDI control channel and the Tone A/B channels the same as your bandmate's unit (MIDI functions 11, 21 and 31).
Turn on sysex (exclusive) in the MIDI functions.
Panel or PG-800 edits go out as sysex parameter messages once sysex is on.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (no USB).
Check both units run the same ROM (stock/V3 or Vecoven V4): their patch formats don't mix.
To send your sound, write it to a patch, then select that patch. It sends the patch plus its tones.
Set the JU-06A's MIDI channel to the one your app uses (Boutique units do this with a button combination at power-on; see the owner's manual).
Nothing to turn on for sysex: the JU-06A doesn't support it, so whole patches can't be sent.
Knob and slider moves go out and come in as CC messages automatically.
Connect with USB or with 5-pin MIDI, not both at once.
To match sounds, both players load the same patch number (Program Change works). Then your knob moves keep them in step.
Set the JP-08's MIDI channel to the one your app uses (Boutique units do this with a button combination at power-on; see the owner's manual).
Nothing to turn on for sysex: the JP-08 doesn't support it, so whole patches can't be sent.
Knob and slider moves go out and come in as CC messages automatically.
Connect with USB or with 5-pin MIDI, not both at once.
To match sounds, both players load the same patch number (Program Change works). Then your knob moves keep them in step.
Set the TB-03's MIDI channel to the one your app uses (Boutique power-on button combination; see the owner's manual).
There's no sysex or Program Change, so the sound can't be sent as a patch.
Knob moves go out and come in as CC messages automatically.
Connect with USB or with 5-pin MIDI, not both at once.
Turn each knob once at the start so your bandmate's TB-03 matches your panel.
Set the SE-02's MIDI channel to the one your app uses (see the owner's manual).
No sysex setting is documented to turn on. Just make sure your app's MIDI OUT reaches the SE-02's MIDI IN or USB.
Knob moves go out and come in as CC messages.
Connect with USB or with 5-pin MIDI, not both at once.
The SE-02 can't send its current sound by itself: turn each knob once to sync, or have both players load the same patch.
Set the TB-3's MIDI channel to the one your app uses (see the owner's manual).
Leave the device ID at its default (17), so the app's requests reach it.
Knob and touch-pad moves go out as CC messages (cutoff, resonance, accent, effect, env mod, tuning).
Use the TB-3's USB port for MIDI, or its MIDI jacks, but not both at once.
If your sound doesn't arrive, the TB-3 may not answer requests. Move each knob once instead.
Set the D-50's basic MIDI channel the same on both units. Its sysex device number follows the channel (channel 1 = 00), so leave it alone.
In the MIDI functions, turn on exclusive (sysex) send and receive.
With exclusive on, panel and PG-1000 edits go out as sysex parameter messages.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (no USB).
If a sound is refused, turn the D-50's memory protect off.
Patches using card tones or voices need the same card in both units.
In SYSTEM, set the MIDI channel for Patch mode the same on both units.
Leave the device ID at its default (17), and turn on receiving exclusive (sysex) in the SYSTEM MIDI settings.
Turn on sending and receiving of edits (sysex) in the SYSTEM MIDI settings, if you want knob moves mirrored.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (no USB).
Put the JV-1080 in PATCH mode (not Performance or GM) before sharing.
Patches using SR-JV80 expansion-board waves need the same board in both units.
In the System parameters under [MIDI PRM], set 'Perform Ctrl CH' to the channel your app uses.
Leave 'Device ID' at 17. Under [MIDI SW], set 'Rx Exclusive SW' to ON.
Under [MIDI SW], set 'Tx/Rx Edit SW' to ON. Set 'Tx/Rx Edit Mode' (MODE1 or MODE2) the same on both units, so knob moves go out and come in.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (no USB).
Share the sound before changing performance: the app reads the current (temporary) performance.
Set the MIDI channel for the part you play the same on both units.
In SYSTEM: MIDI RX, set 'Rx Exclusive' to ON.
Turn 'Transmitted Edit Data' ON so knob edits are sent. Knobs also send CC.
Pick one connection, USB or 5-pin MIDI, and use it on both ends.
Both units should run the same system version.
Set the MIDI channel for each scene part the same on both units (SCENE PART EDIT: MIDI).
In SYSTEM: MIDI RX, set 'Rx Exclusive' to ON.
Knob moves go out as CC; check the SYSTEM: MIDI TX settings are on.
Pick one connection, USB or 5-pin MIDI, and use it on both ends.
Both units should run the same system version (3.0 or later).
Set the TR-8's MIDI channel to the one your app uses (see the owner's manual).
No sysex on the TR-8, so kits and sounds can't be sent as a patch.
Knob moves go out and come in as CC messages. Turn each knob once at the start to sync.
Pick one connection, USB or 5-pin MIDI, and use it on both ends.
Set the TR-8S's MIDI channel to the one your app uses (see the owner's manual).
No sysex on the TR-8S, so kits and sounds can't be sent as a patch.
Knob moves go out and come in as CC messages. Turn each knob once at the start to sync.
Pick one connection, USB or 5-pin MIDI, and use it on both ends.
Have both players pick the same pattern and kit before you start (Program Change selects patterns).
Set the TR-6S's MIDI channel to the one your app uses (see the owner's manual).
No sysex on the TR-6S, so kits and sounds can't be sent as a patch.
Knob moves go out and come in as CC messages. Turn each knob once at the start to sync.
Pick one connection, USB or 5-pin MIDI, and use it on both ends.
Have both players pick the same pattern and kit before you start (Program Change selects patterns).
Set the TR-08's MIDI channel to the one your app uses (see the owner's manual).
No sysex on the TR-08, so kits and sounds can't be sent as a patch.
Knob moves go out and come in as CC messages. Turn each knob once at the start to sync.
Pick one connection, USB or 5-pin MIDI, and use it on both ends.
Set the TR-09's MIDI channel to the one your app uses (see the owner's manual).
No sysex on the TR-09, so kits and sounds can't be sent as a patch.
Knob moves go out and come in as CC messages. Turn each knob once at the start to sync.
Pick one connection, USB or 5-pin MIDI, and use it on both ends.
Set the SP-404MKII's MIDI channel in its MIDI settings (see the owner's manual).
Effect knob moves go out as CC messages.
Pick one connection, USB or 5-pin MIDI, and use it on both ends.
Samples aren't sent over MIDI: both players need the same project loaded.
Set the MC-707's MIDI channels for each track (see the owner's manual).
No sysex, so sounds can't be sent as a patch. Knob moves go out and come in as CC.
Pick one connection, USB or 5-pin MIDI, and use it on both ends.
Both players need the same project loaded (copy it via SD card).
Press EDIT MODE until GLOBAL EDIT shows, press button 4 (GLOBAL 4), and set 'MIDI Ch'. This channel is part of every patch message, so note it in the app.
Sysex is always on; nothing to enable. Just leave 'MIDI Route' (GLOBAL 4) set correctly.
In GLOBAL 5 (button 5), set 'MIDI Tx CC' and 'MIDI Rx CC' to On, so knob moves go out and come in.
In GLOBAL 4 set 'MIDI Route': USB+MIDI uses both the 5-pin jacks and USB; USB uses USB only.
To send the current sound from the panel: EDIT MODE to PROGRAM EDIT, button 8 (DUMP), turn the PROGRAM/VALUE knob to 'Press WRITE', and press WRITE.
Press EDIT MODE until GLOBAL EDIT shows, press button 6 (GLOBAL 4), and set 'MIDI Ch'. This channel is part of every patch message.
Sysex is always on; nothing to enable.
In GLOBAL 5 (button 7), set 'MIDI Tx CC' and 'MIDI Rx CC' to On, so knob moves go out and come in.
In GLOBAL 4 set 'MIDI Route': USB+MIDI uses both the 5-pin jacks and USB; USB uses USB only.
User scales are not part of a program: load the same microtuning on both units if you use one.
To send the current sound from the panel: EDIT MODE to PROGRAM EDIT, button 12 (DUMP), turn the PROGRAM/VALUE knob to 'Press WRITE', and press WRITE.
Press EDIT MODE until GLOBAL EDIT shows, press button 6 (GLOBAL 4), and set 'MIDI Ch'. This channel is part of every patch message.
Sysex is always on; nothing to enable.
In GLOBAL 5 (button 7), set 'MIDI Tx CC' and 'MIDI Rx CC' to On, so knob moves go out and come in.
In GLOBAL 4 set 'MIDI Route': USB+MIDI uses both the 5-pin jacks and USB; USB uses USB only.
If the sound uses a user oscillator or user effect, load the same one into the same slot on both units, and keep the same firmware.
To send the current sound from the panel: EDIT MODE to PROGRAM EDIT, button 14 (DUMP), turn the PROGRAM/VALUE knob to 'Press WRITE', and press WRITE.
Press EDIT MODE until GLOBAL EDIT shows, press button 5 (GLOBAL 5), and set 'MIDI Global Ch'. This channel is part of every patch message.
Sysex is always on; nothing to enable.
In GLOBAL 6 (button 6), set 'MIDI Tx CC' and 'MIDI Rx CC' to On. The sub timbre uses 'MIDI Sub CC Ch' (GLOBAL 5).
In GLOBAL 5 set 'MIDI Route': USB+MIDI uses both the 5-pin jacks and USB; USB uses USB only.
If the sound uses a user oscillator or user effect, load the same one into the same slot on both units.
To send the current sound from the panel: EDIT MODE to FUNCTION, button 7 (DUMP), turn to 'Press WRITE', and press WRITE.
Set the EDIT SELECT 2 dial to MIDI, then use knob 1 ('MIDI CH') to set the channel. This channel is part of every patch message.
Hold SHIFT and press the 4 key (MIDI FILTER), then turn knob 4 (SYSTEM EXCLUSIVE) to Enable.
In the same MIDI FILTER screen, turn knob 2 (CONTROL CHANGE) to Enable, so knob moves go out and come in.
Hold SHIFT and press the 8 key (WRITE PROTECT), then turn knob 1 to OFF, so a received sound is accepted.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (the original microKORG has no USB).
To send the current sound from the panel: hold SHIFT, press the 6 key (MIDI DATA DUMP), turn knob 1 to 1Program, and press the blinking 6 key.
In Global mode, set the global MIDI channel the same on both units. This channel is part of every patch message.
In Global mode, set the system exclusive ('SystemEx') setting to enabled.
Turn memory protect off. Users also report setting MIDI clock to external for dumps to work.
Enable control change transmit and receive in Global mode, so knob moves go out and come in.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (no USB).
Set the DW-8000's MIDI channel the same on both units (MIDI parameters on the panel; see the owner's manual). It's part of every patch message.
Turn on the MIDI exclusive (sysex) setting.
With exclusive on, panel edits go out as sysex parameter messages.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (no USB).
A received sound plays right away but isn't saved until you WRITE it.
In GLOBAL mode, set the global MIDI channel the same on both units. It's part of every patch message.
In GLOBAL mode, turn on system exclusive (sysex) receiving.
Edits can be sent as sysex parameter messages; enable it in GLOBAL mode if you want knob moves mirrored.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (no USB).
Put the M1 in PROGRAM mode (not COMBI) before sharing, and use the same PCM card on both units if the sound needs one.
In Global mode P1: MIDI, set 'MIDI Channel' (the global channel) the same on both units.
In Global P1: MIDI, check 'Enable Exclusive'.
Knob moves are sent as CC or NRPN; check that control change sending is enabled in the Global MIDI settings.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (the Triton has no USB MIDI).
To send the current sound: in Program P0: Play, select the program. With Enable Exclusive checked, the Triton sends it. Save your edits first, because reselecting loses them.
Sounds using EXB-PCM expansion waves or sample RAM need the same on both units.
Press UTILITY, go to MIDI & USB, and set 'Global Channel' the same on both units.
Nothing to enable for patches: the wavestate can't receive a whole program over MIDI.
Assign the Mod Knobs to CCs in UTILITY > MIDI CC Assign, so knob moves go out and come in.
Pick one connection, USB or 5-pin MIDI, and use it on both ends.
Both players load the same program (Program Change via Set Lists) before jamming.
Press UTILITY, go to MIDI & USB, and set 'Global Channel' the same on both units.
Nothing to enable for patches: the modwave can't receive a whole program over MIDI.
Assign the Mod Knobs to CCs in UTILITY > MIDI CC Assign, so knob moves go out and come in.
Pick one connection, USB or 5-pin MIDI, and use it on both ends.
Both players load the same program (Program Change via Set Lists) before jamming.
Hold SHIFT and press EFFECT/GLOBAL, open the MIDI page, and set 'Global Channel'.
Nothing to enable for patches: the opsix can't receive a whole program over MIDI.
On the same MIDI page, set 'Tx CC' and 'Rx CC' on, so knob moves go out and come in.
Pick one connection, USB or 5-pin MIDI, and use it on both ends.
Both players load the same program before jamming (turn 'Rx Prog Chg' and 'Tx Prog Chg' on to follow program changes).
Press Menu/Enter, use < > to show GLOBAL PARAMETER, press Menu/Enter, and set 'GLOBAL MIDI CH' the same on both units.
Set 'MIDI RECEIVE FILTER' and 'MIDI SEND FILTER' to Off, so notes and CC messages get through.
With the filters Off, knob moves go out and come in as CC messages.
Press Write to save the global settings.
A received pattern goes to the current (edit) pattern. Press Write if you want to keep it.
Hold SHIFT and press LIVE to enter Global mode, then press button 7 (MIDI ROUTING) and set the MIDI channel.
No sysex kit transfer, so kits can't be sent as a patch.
In Global mode, set CC to On in button 8 (MIDI RX) and button 9 (MIDI TX), so knob moves go out and come in.
In button 7 set 'ROUTE': USB+MIDI uses both USB and the 5-pin jacks; USB uses USB only.
Both players load the same kit and user units before jamming.
Set the ER-1's MIDI channel (see the owner's manual).
Turn on sending and receiving of control changes, so knob moves are mirrored.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (no USB).
Patterns can't be sent automatically yet: both players load the same pattern.
Hold MEMORY and turn the volca keys on, press the keyboard button for your channel (1-16), then press REC to save.
Hold FUNC and turn it on, make sure keyboard button 7 ('MIDI RX ShortMessage') is lit (On), then press REC.
It has MIDI IN only, so it can receive your bandmate's knob moves (CC) but can't send its own.
Connect a 5-pin MIDI cable to MIDI IN.
Hold MEMORY and turn the volca fm on, press the keyboard button for your channel (1-16), then press REC to save.
Hold FUNC and turn it on, make sure keyboard button 7 ('MIDI RX ShortMessage') is lit (On), then press REC.
It has MIDI IN only, so it can receive your bandmate's knob moves (CC) but can't send its own.
Connect a 5-pin MIDI cable to MIDI IN.
It can load a DX7 voice your bandmate sends from a DX7/DX7II; there's nothing else to set up.
Hold MEMORY and turn the volca bass on, press step button 1-16 for your channel, then press REC to save.
Hold FUNC and turn it on, make sure the 'MIDI RX ShortMessage' step is lit (On; see the global parameter table), then press REC.
It has MIDI IN only, so it can receive knob moves (CC) but can't send its own.
Connect a 5-pin MIDI cable to MIDI IN.
Hold MEMORY and turn the volca beats on, press step button 1-16 for your channel, then press REC to save.
Hold FUNC and turn it on, make sure the 'MIDI RX ShortMessage' step is lit (On; see the global parameter table), then press REC.
It has MIDI IN only, so it can receive knob moves (CC) but can't send its own.
Connect a 5-pin MIDI cable to MIDI IN.
Hold REC and turn the volca drum on, press step button 1-16 for your channel, then press REC. Tap the lit step again to go back to parts 1-6 on channels 1-6.
Hold FUNC and turn it on, make sure the 'MIDI RX ShortMessage' step is lit (On; see the global parameter table), then press REC.
It has MIDI IN only, so it can receive knob moves (CC) but can't send its own.
Connect a 5-pin MIDI cable to MIDI IN.
Each part listens on its own MIDI channel (see the owner's manual for the part-to-channel table).
Hold FUNC and turn the volca sample on, make sure step 7 ('MIDI RX ShortMessage') is lit, then press REC.
It has MIDI IN only, so it can receive knob moves (CC) but can't send its own.
Connect a 5-pin MIDI cable to MIDI IN. Samples are not sent over MIDI, so both players need the same samples loaded.
Press FUNCTION, then 8, and set the MIDI channel. The sysex device number follows this channel.
In function 8, set SYS INFO AVAIL, so the DX7 sends and accepts voice data.
With SYS INFO AVAIL, data-entry slider edits go out as sysex parameter messages.
On the receiving DX7, turn INTERNAL MEMORY PROTECT off, or it may refuse the sound.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (no USB).
To send your sound: store your edit to a voice, then select that voice. With SYS INFO AVAIL the DX7 sends it.
Set the MIDI receive and transmit channel the same on both units. The device number follows the channel.
Set MIDI IN to 'normal' (button 29), or the DX7II silently ignores sysex.
Turn memory protect off (button 14) on the receiving unit.
Turn on sysex parameter sending in the MIDI settings if you want edits mirrored.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (no USB).
Set the DX21's MIDI receive and transmit channel the same on both units. The device number follows the channel.
Turn MIDI SYS INFO ON, so it answers requests and sends edits as sysex.
With MIDI SYS INFO ON, panel edits go out as sysex parameter messages.
Turn MEMORY PROTECT off on the receiving unit if a sound is refused.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (no USB).
Set the DX100's MIDI receive and transmit channel the same on both units. The device number follows the channel.
Turn MIDI SYS INFO ON, so it answers requests and sends edits as sysex.
With MIDI SYS INFO ON, panel edits go out as sysex parameter messages.
Turn MEMORY PROTECT off on the receiving unit if a sound is refused.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (no USB).
Set 'Basic Rx channel' and 'Transmit channel' to the same MIDI channel (usually 1).
In UTILITY > MIDI Control, set 'Exclusive' to On.
With Exclusive on, edits are sent as sysex parameter messages.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (no USB).
Share a single voice: performance settings (PCED) aren't included in the sound.
Set the FS1R's performance MIDI channel and the sysex device number the same on both units (device 1 is the default).
Turn on sysex receive in the system MIDI settings.
Edits are sent as sysex parameter messages when sysex is on.
Connect with 5-pin MIDI cables (no USB).
Fseq data and preset voices aren't sent; both units need them loaded.
Set the reface DX's MIDI channel the same on both units (see the owner's manual).
Sysex needs no setup the app knows of. If a sound is refused, check the MIDI settings in the reface DX owner's manual.
Panel edits go out over MIDI; check that MIDI control is on in the reface's settings.
Use the USB port or the MIDI port (with its breakout cable), but not both at once.
Set the Montage's MIDI channel in its Utility MIDI settings.
Knob and slider moves go out and come in as CC or NRPN messages; check control change sending is on.
Pick one connection, USB or 5-pin MIDI, and use it on both ends.
Patches can't be sent automatically yet: both players load the same Performance (and libraries).
